name: starter-table-stock
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: The MIRROR IMAGE of starter-table-proofhack.json: the same probes, the same controls, the same liveness assertions -- only the two discriminating expected values differ. It asserts the STOCK sStarterMon values (TORCHIC in the middle), so it PASSes on pokemon/engine/pokeemerald.gba and MUST FAIL on pokemon/hacks/proofhack/pokeemerald.gba. Running both specs against both ROMs gives a 2x2 matrix whose diagonal is PASS and whose off-diagonal is FAIL. One direction alone would be a weaker claim: a spec that fails on the stock ROM might merely be a spec that fails. Failing in the OTHER direction too, on the same probes, is what rules that out.

probes.why: THE WHOLE TABLE, as raw bytes. static const u16 sStarterMon[3] at src/starter_choose.c:113, little-endian: fc00 ff00 0201 = TREECKO(252) TORCHIC(255) MUDKIP(258). Exact byte-string compare -- the check class doc 55 §9.4 found actually discriminates, as against thresholds and constant checks which do not.
THE ONE CHANGED VALUE, from the other side. sStarterMon[1]: SPECIES_TORCHIC = 255 here. proofhack rebuilt it as SPECIES_CHARMANDER = 4, so this assertion is the one that flips.
CONTROL. sStarterMon[0] = SPECIES_TREECKO = 252 in BOTH builds. Its PASSing on the hack is what shows the FAIL is aimed at the edited element rather than at 'this is a different binary'.

CONTROL, other side. sStarterMon[2] = SPECIES_MUDKIP = 258 in both builds. 258 = 0x0102 is the one value here whose two bytes differ, so a mis-sized or mis-offset read is visible rather than silently agreeing.
gMain.vblankCounter1 (include/main.h offset 0x20). The table reads come from a machine that was executing, not from a file on disk.
gMain.callback2 (offset 0x04), resolved against the .sym of the ROM actually under test.

assert.why: DISCRIMINATOR 1. The stock starter table, exact bytes. On the proofhack ROM this reads fc0004000201 and FAILS.
DISCRIMINATOR 2, isolated to the one element so the failure names the slot. SPECIES_TORCHIC = 255 (include/constants/species.h:259). On proofhack this reads 4 and FAILS.
SUPPORTING ONLY -- never load-bearing. Doc 55 §9.4: constant survives an address shift because garbage is unchanging too.
CONTROL. Must PASS on BOTH builds.
CONTROL, other side. Must PASS on BOTH builds.
Every sample of the table was readable.
The table was re-read many times across the run, not once at a lucky moment.
The engine was alive and advancing for the whole run.
Every non-null callback resolves in this build's own .sym; zero at frame 1 is legitimate.
Doc 54 §3's boot progression, asserted by name. Because this holds on BOTH builds, a FAIL of this spec on the hack cannot be explained away as 'the hack does not boot'.
